sentences.zh: ○李抱玉　李抱真　王虔休　盧從史　李芃李澄 族弟元素李抱玉李抱玉，武德功臣安興貴之裔。

translations.literal: ○ Li Baoyu, Li Baozhen, Wang Qianxiu, Lu Congshi, Li Peng, Li Cheng, and his clansman cousin Yuan Su. Li Baoyu was a descendant of An Xinggui, a meritorious minister of the Wude reign.
translations.idiomatic: ○ Li Baoyu, Li Baozhen, Wang Qianxiu, Lu Congshi, Li Peng, Li Cheng, and his clansman Yuan Su. Li Baoyu traced his line to An Xinggui, one of the founding heroes of the Wude era.

sentences.zh: 代居河西，善養名馬，為時所稱。

translations.literal: For generations they dwelt in Hexi, skilled at raising famous horses, and were praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: The family had lived in Hexi for generations, renowned for breeding fine horses.

sentences.zh: 群從兄弟，或徙居京華，習文儒，與士人通婚者，稍染士風。

translations.literal: Among the collateral brothers, some moved to the capital, studied letters and Confucian learning, and intermarried with scholar-officials, gradually taking on the air of the literati.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his kinsmen moved to the capital, took up literary studies, and married into gentry families, slowly acquiring the manners of scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 抱玉少長西州，好騎射，常從軍幕，沉毅有謀，小心忠謹。

translations.literal: Baoyu grew up from youth in Xizhou, loved mounted archery, often followed military staffs, was deep-steadied and resourceful, careful, loyal, and conscientious.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu had grown up in Xizhou, loved horsemanship and archery, and spent much of his youth in army camps—steady, shrewd, and scrupulously loyal.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，太尉李光弼引為偏裨，屢建勳績，由是知名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era, Grand Marshal Li Guangbi brought him in as a junior officer; he repeatedly achieved merit and thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianyuan era, Grand Marshal Li Guangbi took him on as a staff officer; repeated battlefield successes soon made his name known.

sentences.zh: 二年，自特進、右羽林軍大將軍、知軍事，遷鴻臚卿員外置同正員，持節鄭州諸軍事兼鄭州刺史、攝御史中丞、鄭陳潁亳四州節度。

translations.literal: In the second year, from Special Grand Tutor, Grand General of the Right Bulwark Forest Army with military authority, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Receptions Service with acting full title, bearing the staff as military commissioner of all Zhengzhou forces and concurrently Prefect of Zhengzhou, acting Vice Censor-in-chief, and military commissioner of the four prefectures Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he rose from Special Grand Tutor and Grand General of the Right Imperial Guard, with command of military affairs, to Vice Director of the Palace Receptions Service (acting full rank), and was commissioned to oversee Zhengzhou’s armies while serving as prefect, acting Vice Censor-in-chief, and military commissioner over Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.

sentences.zh: 時史思明陷洛陽，光弼守河陽，賊兵鋒方盛，光弼謂抱玉曰：「將軍能為我守南城二日乎？

translations.literal: At that time Shi Siming had taken Luoyang; Guangbi held Heyang; rebel spearheads were at their height. Guangbi said to Baoyu: "General, can you hold the south city for me for two days?
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming had seized Luoyang while Guangbi held Heyang; rebel forces were at their peak. Guangbi asked Baoyu, "Can you hold the south wall for two days?

sentences.zh: 」抱玉曰：「過期若何？

translations.literal: " Baoyu said: "If the deadline passes, then what?
translations.idiomatic: " Baoyu asked, "And if the two days pass?

sentences.zh: 」光弼曰：「過期而救不至，任棄城也。

translations.literal: " Guangbi said: "If the deadline passes and rescue does not arrive, you may abandon the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Guangbi replied, "If relief has not come by then, you may abandon the city.

sentences.zh: 」賊帥周摯領安太清、徐黃玉等先次南城，將陷之，抱玉乃紿之曰：「吾糧盡，明日當降。

translations.literal: " The rebel commander Zhou Zhi, leading An Taiqing, Xu Huangyu, and others, first reached the south city and was about to take it. Baoyu then deceived them, saying: "Our grain is exhausted; tomorrow we shall surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " Rebel commander Zhou Zhi, with An Taiqing, Xu Huangyu, and others, reached the south city first and was poised to storm it. Baoyu deceived them: "Our provisions are gone—we will surrender tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」賊眾大喜，斂軍以俟之。

translations.literal: " The rebel masses were greatly pleased and drew in their forces to wait.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels were delighted and held their troops back to wait.

sentences.zh: 抱玉因得繕完設備，明日，堅壁請戰。

translations.literal: Baoyu thereby was able to repair and complete his defenses and equipment; the next day he held the walls fast and asked for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu used the respite to repair the walls and stock supplies; the next day he shut the gates and challenged them to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊怒欺紿，急攻之。

translations.literal: The rebels, furious at being deceived, pressed the attack urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged at the trick, the rebels assaulted the walls at once.

sentences.zh: 抱玉出奇兵，表裡夾攻，殺傷甚眾，摯軍退。

translations.literal: Baoyu sent out unusual troops; inside and outside they attacked from both sides, killing and wounding a great many; Zhi's army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu sent out ambush troops to strike from within and without; casualties were heavy, and Zhi’s force retreated.

sentences.zh: 光弼自將於中潬城，摯舍南城攻中潬，不勝，乃整軍將攻北城。

translations.literal: Guangbi himself led at Zhongtan city; Zhi left the south city to attack Zhongtan, could not win, then massed his army intending to attack the north city.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi commanded from Zhongtan; Zhi abandoned the south city to attack Zhongtan, failed, then regrouped to strike the north wall.

sentences.zh: 光弼以兵出戰，大敗之。

translations.literal: Guangbi led troops out to battle and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Guangbi marched out and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 固河陽，復懷州，皆功居第一，遷澤州刺史、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In securing Heyang and recovering Huaizhou, his merit ranked first; he was promoted Prefect of Zezhou and concurrently Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked first in merit for holding Heyang and retaking Huaizhou, and was made prefect of Zezhou with the concurrent title of Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 代宗即位，擢為澤潞節度使、潞州大都督府長史、兼御史大夫，加領陳、鄭二州，遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong took the throne, he was elevated to military commissioner of Ze and Lu, Chief Administrator of the Lu Metropolitan Prefecture, concurrently Censor-in-chief, additionally given Chen and Zheng prefectures, and moved to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Daizong succeeded, Baoyu was appointed military commissioner of Ze and Lu, chief administrator of Lu prefecture, and Censor-in-chief, with added authority over Chen and Zheng, and later became Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 抱玉上言：「臣貫屬涼州，本姓安氏，以祿山構禍，恥與同姓，去至德二年五月，蒙恩賜姓李氏，今請割貫屬京兆府長安縣。

translations.literal: Baoyu submitted memorial: "Your subject was long registered to Liangzhou; originally surname An. Because Lu Shan wrought calamity, I am ashamed to share the surname; in the fifth month of the second year of Zhide I received grace and was granted surname Li. Now I request to be severed from registration and attached to Chang'an county of Jingzhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu memorialized: "I was long registered in Liangzhou and bore the surname An. After An Lushan’s rebellion I was ashamed to share that name; in the fifth month of Zhide 2 the throne granted me the surname Li. I now ask to be registered in Chang’an county, Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 」許之，因是舉宗並賜國姓。

translations.literal: " It was granted; thereby his whole clan was also granted the imperial surname.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved, and his entire clan received the imperial surname as well.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年冬，吐蕃寇京師，乘輿幸陝，諸軍潰卒及村閭亡命相聚為盜，京城南面子午等五穀群盜頗害居人，朝廷遣薛景仙領兵為五穀使招討，連月不捷，乃詔抱玉兼鳳翔節度使討之。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Guangde, Tibetans raided the capital; the imperial carriage went to Shan; scattered troops and village desperados gathered as bandits. South of the capital at Ziwu and the other Five Valleys, bandit gangs greatly harmed residents. The court sent Xue Jingxian to lead troops as commissioner of the Five Valleys to pacify them; for months he had no success. Then Baoyu was ordered concurrently as Fengxiang military commissioner to subdue them.
translations.idiomatic: That winter of Guangde 1 Tibetans raided the capital and the emperor withdrew to Shan. Routed soldiers and village outlaws formed bandit bands; south of Chang’an, in the Ziwu and other Five Valleys, gangs preyed on civilians. Xue Jingxian led a pacification force for months without success, so Baoyu was ordered to take Fengxiang and crush them.

sentences.zh: 抱玉探知賊帥行止之處，先分屯諸谷，乃設奇潛使輕銳數百南自洋州入攻之。

translations.literal: Baoyu learned where the bandit chiefs went and came; first he stationed troops separately in the various valleys, then set an ambush and secretly sent several hundred light crack troops south from Yang prefecture to attack.
translations.idiomatic: After learning where the chiefs were operating, he posted troops in the valleys, then sent several hundred picked men south from Yangzhou in a surprise strike.

sentences.zh: 賊帥高玉方與諸偷會，遽為銳卒數十人掩擒之，因大搜獲偷黨，悉斬之，餘黨不討自潰，旬日內五穀平。

translations.literal: Bandit chief Gao Yu was just meeting with various robbers when suddenly several dozen crack soldiers seized him by surprise; they then searched widely and captured robber partisans, all beheaded; the remaining partisans dispersed without pursuit; within ten days the Five Valleys were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Gao Yu was meeting his fellows when a few dozen raiders seized him; a sweep captured the rest and beheaded them. The remnant bands melted away, and within ten days the Five Valleys were quiet.

sentences.zh: 以功遷司空，余並如故。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Minister of Works; the remainder unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to Minister of Works; his other posts remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃每歲犯境，上以岐陽國之西門，寄在抱玉，恩寵無比，遷同中書門下平章事，又兼山南西道節度使、河西隴右山南西道副元帥、判梁州事，連統三道節制，兼領鳳翔、潞、梁三大府，秩處三公。

translations.literal: At that time Tibetans annually raided the borders; the emperor regarded Qiyang as the western gate of the state and entrusted it to Baoyu; favor was without parallel. He was promoted concurrent co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, also military commissioner of the Huainan west circuit, deputy grand marshal of Hexi, Longyou, and Huainan west, and judged Liangzhou affairs; he commanded three circuits in succession, concurrently held the three great prefectures Fengxiang, Lu, and Liang, and his rank stood at the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Tibetans raided the frontier every year; the emperor treated Qiyang as the realm’s western gate and placed it in Baoyu’s hands with unmatched favor. He became a co-director of the Secretariat, deputy grand marshal over Hexi, Longyou, and the Huainan west circuit, and administrator of Liangzhou—commanding three circuits and three major prefectures at a rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 抱玉以任位崇重，抗疏懇讓司空及山南西道節度、判梁州事，乞退授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Baoyu, because his duties and position were lofty and heavy, submitted a forthright memorial earnestly declining the Minister of Works post and the Huainan west military commission and judging of Liangzhou, asking to step back to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his posts too weighty, Baoyu petitioned to relinquish Minister of Works, the Huainan west commission, and Liangzhou administration, asking only to remain Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其謙讓，許之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his modesty and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his modesty and agreed.

sentences.zh: 抱雲凡鎮鳳翔十餘年，雖無破虜之功，而禁暴安人，頗為當時所稱。

translations.literal: Baoyu in all governed Fengxiang for more than ten years; though he had no merit in destroying the enemy, in suppressing violence and settling the people he was much praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyu governed Fengxiang for more than ten years. He won no great victories over foreign foes, but his suppression of lawlessness and care for the people won wide praise.

sentences.zh: 大曆十二年卒，上甚悼之，輟朝三日，贈太保。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Dali he died; the emperor greatly mourned him, halted court for three days, and posthumously granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Dali 12. The emperor mourned deeply, suspended court for three days, and posthumously named him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 李抱真李抱真，抱玉從父弟也。

translations.literal: Li Baozhen. Li Baozhen was Baoyu's cousin on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen was Baoyu’s paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 抱玉為澤潞節度使，甚器抱真，任以軍事，累授汾州別駕。

translations.literal: When Baoyu was military commissioner of Ze and Lu, he greatly valued Baozhen, entrusted him with military affairs, and repeatedly appointed him acting prefect of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: While Baoyu held Ze and Lu, he relied heavily on Baozhen for military affairs and repeatedly named him acting prefect of Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 當是時，僕固懷恩反於汾州，抱真陷焉，乃脫身歸京師。

translations.literal: At that time Pugu Huai'en rebelled at Fenzhou; Baozhen was trapped there, then escaped and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai’en rebelled at Fenzhou, Baozhen was caught up in the revolt but broke free and reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗以懷恩倚回紇，所將朔方兵又勁，憂甚，召見抱真問狀，因奏曰：「郭子儀領朔方之眾，人多思之。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong, because Huai'en relied on the Uyghurs and the Shuofang troops he led were also strong, was deeply worried; he summoned Baozhen and asked the situation; he thereupon memorialized: "Guo Ziyi leads the Shuofang masses; many long for him.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong, alarmed that Huai’en had Uyghur backing and commanded the formidable Shuofang army, summoned Baozhen and asked what he knew. Baozhen replied, "Guo Ziyi still commands the Shuofang troops in the soldiers’ hearts.

sentences.zh: 懷恩欺其眾，曰『子儀為朝恩所殺』，詐而用之。

translations.literal: Huai'en deceives the masses, saying 'Ziyi was killed by court grudge,' and uses them by fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Huai’en deceives them, claiming ‘Ziyi was murdered by court intrigue,’ and leads them by that lie.

sentences.zh: 今復子儀之位，可不戰而克。

translations.literal: Now restore Ziyi's post and you can conquer without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Restore Ziyi to command and the rebellion will collapse without a fight.

sentences.zh: 」其後懷恩子瑒為其下所殺，懷恩奔遁，多如抱真策，因是遷殿中少監。

translations.literal: " Afterward Huai'en's son Chang was killed by his subordinates; Huai'en fled in flight; much went as Baozhen had strategized; thereby he was moved to Junior Supervisor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: " Huai’en’s son Chang was later killed by his own men; Huai’en fled—much as Baozhen had predicted—and Baozhen was promoted to Junior Supervisor of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 居頃之，為陳鄭、澤潞節度留後，抱真因中謝言曰：「臣雖無可取，當今百姓勞逸，系在牧守，願得一郡以自試。

translations.literal: After a short while he became acting military commissioner of Chen, Zheng, Ze, and Lu. Baozhen, when presenting thanks at court, said: "Your subject though has nothing to be taken, yet today the people's toil and ease depend on the prefects and commissioners; I wish to receive one commandery to try myself.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became acting commissioner of Chen, Zheng, Ze, and Lu. When he thanked the throne, Baozhen said, "I have little to offer, but the people’s welfare rests on their governors; grant me one prefecture to prove myself.

sentences.zh: 」上許之，改授澤州刺史，兼為澤潞節度副使。

translations.literal: " The emperor granted it and changed his appointment to Prefect of Zezhou, concurrently Vice military commissioner of Ze and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and named him prefect of Zezhou and deputy commissioner of Ze and Lu.

sentences.zh: 居二年，轉懷州刺史，復為懷澤潞觀察使留後，凡八年。

translations.literal: After two years he was transferred to Prefect of Huaizhou, again acting commissioner of the Huai, Ze, and Lu observation circuit; in all eight years.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became prefect of Huaizhou and again acting commissioner of the Huai–Ze–Lu circuit—for eight years in all.

sentences.zh: 抱玉卒，抱真仍領留後。

translations.literal: When Baoyu died, Baozhen still held the acting commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyu died, Baozhen remained as acting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 抱真密揣山東當有變，上黨且當兵沖，是時乘戰余之地，土瘠賦重，人益困，無以養軍士。

translations.literal: Baozhen secretly judged that Shandong would have upheaval and Shangdang would be a military choke point; at that time it was land worn by war, soil lean and taxes heavy, people increasingly distressed, with no means to support soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen sensed trouble brewing in the east: Shangdang would become a battleground. The region was war-ravaged, the soil poor and taxes heavy; the people were exhausted and could not sustain an army.

sentences.zh: 籍戶丁男，三選其一，有材力者免其租徭，給弓矢，令之曰：「農之隙，則分曹角射；

translations.literal: He registered household adult males, choosing one in three; those with strength and talent were exempted from rent and corvée, given bows and arrows, and ordered: "In the gaps of farming, then divide into groups and compete in archery;
translations.idiomatic: He registered every third able-bodied man, exempted the strong from taxes and corvée, issued bows, and ordered: "In slack farming seasons, drill by squads in archery;

sentences.zh: 歲終，吾當會試。

translations.literal: at year's end I shall hold a joint examination.
translations.idiomatic: at year’s end I will hold a muster and examination.

sentences.zh: 」及期，按簿而征之，都試以示賞罰，覆命之如初。

translations.literal: " When the term came, according to the registers he summoned them, held a collective examination to show reward and punishment, and repeated the order as at first.
translations.idiomatic: " When the season came he called them up by register, held a general review with rewards and penalties, and renewed the order for the next year.

sentences.zh: 比三年，則皆善射，抱真曰：「軍可用矣。

translations.literal: By three years, all were skilled at shooting; Baozhen said: "The army can be used.
translations.idiomatic: Within three years they were all crack archers. Baozhen said, "The army is ready.

sentences.zh: 」於是舉部內鄉兵，得成卒二萬，前既不廩費，府庫益實，乃繕甲兵，為戰具，遂雄視山東。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he raised militia within the command, obtaining twenty thousand trained soldiers; previously there had been no granary expense, the treasury grew fuller, then he repaired armor and weapons and made battle gear, and thereby dominated Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: " He then mobilized local militia into twenty thousand regular troops. Having spent nothing from the granaries, his treasury grew rich; he outfitted armor and weapons and came to dominate the east.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下稱昭義軍步兵冠諸軍。

translations.literal: At that time the realm said the Zhaoyi Army's infantry topped all armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Zhaoyi infantry were reckoned the finest in the empire.

sentences.zh: 無幾，復代李承昭為昭義軍及磁邢節度觀察留後，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Before long he again replaced Li Chengzhao as acting military commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army and observation commissioner of Ci and Xing, with added title Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he succeeded Li Chengzhao as acting commissioner of the Zhaoyi Army and the Ci–Xing circuit, with the added title of Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 德宗即位，拜檢校工部尚書，兼潞州長史、昭義軍節度支度營田、澤潞磁邢觀察使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, he was appointed Acting Minister of Works, concurrently Chief Administrator of Lu prefecture, Zhaoyi Army military commissioner with supply, finance, and garrison fields, and observation commissioner of Ze, Lu, Ci, and Xing.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded, Baozhen was named Acting Minister of Works, chief administrator of Lu, Zhaoyi military commissioner with control of supplies and garrison lands, and observation commissioner over Ze, Lu, Ci, and Xing.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，田悅以魏博反，乃悉兵圍邢州及臨洺益急，詔河東節度使馬燧及神策兵救之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong, Tian Yue rebelled with Weibo and mustered all troops to besiege Xingzhou and Linming with increasing urgency; an edict ordered Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui and the Shence troops to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2 Tian Yue rebelled in Weibo and pressed the siege of Xingzhou and Linming. Ma Sui of Hedong and the Shence guards were ordered to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 抱真與燧敗悅兵於雙岡，斬悅將楊朝光，又擊破悅於臨洺，遂解臨洺及邢州之圍，以功加檢校兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Baozhen with Sui defeated Yue's troops at Shuanggang, beheaded Yue's general Yang Chaoguang, again routed Yue at Linming, and thereby lifted the sieges of Linming and Xingzhou; for merit he was added Acting Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen and Ma Sui routed Tian Yue at Shuanggang, killed his general Yang Chaoguang, defeated him again at Linming, and lifted both sieges; Baozhen was promoted to Acting Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 復與燧大破悅於洹水，悅以數百騎走歸魏州。

translations.literal: Again with Sui he greatly defeated Yue at the Huan River; Yue fled with several hundred horsemen back to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Sui he again crushed Tian Yue on the Huan River; Yue fled to Weizhou with a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 復與燧圍魏州，又敗悅於城下，以功加檢校右僕射。

translations.literal: Again with Sui he besieged Weizhou and again defeated Yue below the walls; for merit he was added Acting Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Weizhou and defeated Yue again beneath the walls; Baozhen was made Acting Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 時悅窘蹙，硃滔、王武俊皆反，聯兵救悅，抱真與燧等退次魏縣。

translations.literal: At that time Yue was hard pressed; Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun both rebelled and joined forces to rescue Yue; Baozhen with Sui and others withdrew and encamped at Weixian.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yue was cornered, but Zhu Tao and Wang Wujun rebelled and marched to his aid; Baozhen and Ma Sui fell back to Weixian.

sentences.zh: 上幸奉天，中使告問至，諸將皆仰天慟哭。

translations.literal: The emperor went to Fengtian; palace envoys bearing inquiries arrived; all the generals looked to heaven and wept bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to Fengtian; when palace envoys brought word, the generals wept aloud to heaven.

sentences.zh: 李懷光席捲奔命，馬燧、李芃各引兵歸鎮。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang swept along in desperate haste; Ma Sui and Li Peng each led troops back to their commands.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai’guang rushed off in haste; Ma Sui and Li Peng each withdrew to their own circuits.

sentences.zh: 硃泚既汙宮闕，時李希烈陷大梁，李納亦反鄆州。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci had already defiled the palace precincts; at that time Li Xilie had taken Daliang; Li Na also rebelled at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci had seized the capital; Li Xilie held Daliang; Li Na rebelled in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 無何，上幸梁州，李懷光又竊據河中。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor went to Liangzhou; Li Huai'guang again secretly seized Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the emperor withdrew to Liangzhou, and Li Huai’guang seized Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 抱真獨於擾攘傾潰之中，以山東三州外抗群賊，內輯軍士，群賊深憚之。

translations.literal: Baozhen alone amid turmoil and collapsing ruin, with the three Shandong prefectures outward resisted the mass of rebels and inward disciplined the soldiers; the mass of rebels deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Alone amid chaos, Baozhen held three eastern prefectures, fought the rebel hosts without, and kept his army in order within; the rebels feared him deeply.

sentences.zh: 興元初，遷檢校左僕射、平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xingyuan he was moved to Acting Left Vice Director and Co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xingyuan era he became Acting Left Vice Director and a co-director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時硃滔悉幽薊軍，借兵回紇，擁眾五萬，南向以應泚，攻圍貝州。

translations.literal: At that time Zhu Tao mustered all the You and Ji armies, borrowed Uyghur troops, and with a host of fifty thousand marched south to respond to Ci, attacking and besieging Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao gathered the You–Ji armies, borrowed Uyghur auxiliaries, and marched south with fifty thousand men to support Zhu Ci, besieging Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，群賊附於希烈，希烈僭偽，有臣屬群賊意，群心稍離。

translations.literal: At first the mass of rebels attached to Xilie; Xilie usurped falsely and had the mind to make the mass of rebels his subjects; their hearts gradually parted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders had rallied to Li Xilie, but when he declared himself emperor and treated them as vassals, their loyalty began to fray.

sentences.zh: 上自奉天下罪己之詔，悉赦群賊，抱真乃遣門客賈林以大義說武俊，合從擊硃滔，武俊許之。

translations.literal: The emperor from Fengtian issued the self-blame edict to the realm, pardoning all the mass of rebels; Baozhen then sent his retainer guest Jia Lin with great righteousness to persuade Wujun to ally and strike Zhu Tao; Wujun agreed.
translations.idiomatic: From Fengtian the emperor issued his self-reproach edict and pardoned the rebels. Baozhen sent his client Jia Lin to persuade Wang Wujun by righteous argument to join against Zhu Tao, and Wujun agreed.

sentences.zh: 時兩軍尚相疑，抱真乃以數騎徑入武俊營。

translations.literal: At that time the two armies still mutually suspected; Baozhen then with several horsemen went straight into Wujun's camp.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies still distrusted each other, so Baozhen rode into Wujun’s camp with only a few escorts.

sentences.zh: 其將去也，賓客皆止之，抱真遣軍司馬盧玄卿勒軍部分曰：「僕今日此舉，系天下安危。

translations.literal: As he was about to go, all the guests restrained him; Baozhen sent Army Vice Director Lu Xuanqing to array the army sections, saying: "My lord's act today bears on the realm's safety and peril.
translations.idiomatic: His staff tried to stop him. Baozhen sent his army vice director Lu Xuanqing to address the troops: "What I do today concerns the fate of the empire.

sentences.zh: 僕死不還，領軍事以聽朝命，亦唯子；

translations.literal: If my lord does not return in death, take command of military affairs and heed court orders—that too is only you;
translations.idiomatic: If I do not return, take command and obey the court—that duty is yours alone;

sentences.zh: 奮勵士馬，東向雪僕之恥，亦唯子。

translations.literal: rouse the soldiers and horses, march east to wipe away my lord's shame—that too is only you.
translations.idiomatic: and rouse the army to march east and avenge my disgrace—that too rests on you alone.

sentences.zh: 」言訖而去。

translations.literal: " Having spoken, he departed.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he rode off.

sentences.zh: 武俊設備甚嚴，抱真曰：「硃泚、希烈僭竊大位，硃滔攻圍貝州，此輩皆欲陵駕吾屬。

translations.literal: Wujun made preparations very strict; Baozhen said: "Zhu Ci and Xilie usurped the great throne; Zhu Tao attacks and besieges Beizhou—these men all wish to ride over us.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun had taken strict precautions. Baozhen said, "Zhu Ci and Li Xilie have seized imperial titles; Zhu Tao besieges Beizhou—all of them mean to dominate us.

sentences.zh: 足下既不能自振數賊之上，舍九葉天子而北面臣反虜乎？

translations.literal: Your excellency, if you cannot raise yourself above several rebels, will you abandon the nine-generation Son of Heaven and face north to serve rebel captives?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot stand above these rebels, will you abandon the Son of Heaven of nine generations and bow north to traitors?

sentences.zh: 乃者聖上奉天下罪己之詔，可謂禹、湯之主也。

translations.literal: Recently the sage emperor issued to the realm the self-blame edict—he may be called a lord like Yu and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has just issued his self-reproach edict to the realm—a ruler in the mold of Yu and Tang.

sentences.zh: 」因言及播越，持武俊哭，涕泗交下，武俊亦哭，感動左右。

translations.literal: " Then speaking of the imperial flight, he seized Wujun and wept; tears and mucus crossed down; Wujun also wept, moving those at his side.
translations.idiomatic: " He spoke of the emperor’s exile, seized Wujun, and wept until both men were in tears, moving everyone present.

sentences.zh: 因退臥武俊帳中，酣寢久之。

translations.literal: Then he withdrew and lay down in Wujun's tent, sleeping soundly for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He then retired to Wujun’s tent and slept deeply for a long time.

sentences.zh: 武俊感其不疑，待之益恭，指心仰天曰：「此身已許公死敵矣。

translations.literal: Wujun, moved by his lack of suspicion, treated him ever more respectfully, pointed to his heart and looked to heaven, saying: "This body is already pledged to my lord to die against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by such trust, Wujun treated him with still greater respect, pointed to his heart, and swore to heaven, "I have pledged my life to fight your enemies.

sentences.zh: 」遂與結為兄弟而別，約明日合戰，遂擊破硃滔於經城，以功加檢校司空，實封五百戶。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they became sworn brothers and parted, agreeing to join battle the next day; then they routed Zhu Tao at Jingcheng; for merit he was added Acting Minister of Works with a substantive fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: " They swore brotherhood and parted, agreeing to fight together the next day. They defeated Zhu Tao at Jingcheng; Baozhen was made Acting Minister of Works with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，朝於京師，居頃之，還鎮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he attended court at the capital; after a short while he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era he visited the capital, then soon returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 抱真沉斷多智計，嘗欲招致天下賢俊，聞人之善，必令持貨幣數千里邀致之；

translations.literal: Baozhen was deep, decisive, and full of stratagems; he once wished to summon the realm's worthy and eminent; hearing of someone's excellence, he always sent men bearing goods and currency for thousands of li to invite and bring them;
translations.idiomatic: Baozhen was shrewd and resolute. He sought to gather talented men from across the empire; whenever he heard of someone’s merit, he sent agents with gifts thousands of li to fetch them;

sentences.zh: 至與語無可採者，漸退之。

translations.literal: when upon speaking with them there was nothing to be gathered, he gradually sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: but if conversation proved unrewarding, he quietly let them go.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，乃大起台榭，穿池沼以自娛。

translations.literal: When the realm was without affairs, he greatly raised terraces and pavilions and dug ponds for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: When the realm was at peace he built pavilions and dug ponds for his amusement.

sentences.zh: 晚節又好方士，以冀長生。

translations.literal: In his later years he again favored alchemical masters, hoping for long life.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned to Daoist adepts, hoping for immortality.

sentences.zh: 有孫季長者，為抱真練金丹，紿抱真曰：「服之當升仙」遂署為賓僚。

translations.literal: There was Sun Jichang, who for Baozhen refined golden elixir pills, deceived Baozhen saying: "If you take them you will ascend as immortal," and he was then appointed among the guest staff.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Sun Jichang prepared elixir pills for him and promised ascension if he took them; Baozhen made him a personal adviser.

sentences.zh: 數謂參佐曰：「此丹秦皇、漢武皆不能得，唯我遇之，他年朝上清，不復偶公輩矣。

translations.literal: He repeatedly told his aides: "This elixir even Qin Huangdi and Han Wudi could not obtain; only I have encountered it; in future years I shall attend the Upper Clarity and no longer keep company with you gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He often told his staff, "Even the First Emperor and Han Wudi never obtained this elixir—only I have. One day I shall ascend to the heavens and leave you behind.

sentences.zh: 」復夢駕鶴衝天，寤而刻木鶴、衣道士衣以習乘之。

translations.literal: " Again he dreamed of riding a crane soaring to heaven; waking, he carved a wooden crane, put on a Daoist priest's robe, and practiced riding it.
translations.idiomatic: " He dreamed of riding a crane to heaven, then carved a wooden crane, donned Daoist robes, and practiced mounting it.

sentences.zh: 凡服丹二萬丸，腹堅不食，將死，不知人者數日矣。

translations.literal: In all he took twenty thousand pills; his belly hardened and he did not eat; as death approached he did not know people for several days.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed twenty thousand pills until his belly hardened and he stopped eating; for days before death he recognized no one.

sentences.zh: 道士牛洞玄以豬肪谷漆下之，殆盡。

translations.literal: The Daoist priest Niu Dongxuan used pig fat and grain lacquer to purge him down; he was nearly finished.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Niu Dongxuan purged him with pig fat and grain lacquer until he was nearly dead.

sentences.zh: 病少間，季長復曰：「垂上仙，何自棄也！

translations.literal: When his illness eased a little, Jichang again said: "On the verge of ascending as immortal, why abandon it yourself!
translations.idiomatic: When he briefly recovered, Jichang said, "You are on the verge of immortality—why throw that away!

sentences.zh: 」益服三千丸，頃之卒。

translations.literal: " He took three thousand more pills; shortly he died.
translations.idiomatic: " Baozhen took three thousand more pills and soon died.

sentences.zh: 初，抱真久疾，好禨祥，或令厭勝，為巫祝所惑，請降官爵以禳除之。

translations.literal: At first, when Baozhen had long been ill, he loved omens and auspicious signs, sometimes ordered exorcistic suppression, was deluded by shamans and prayer masters, and requested to lower rank and titles to expel and remove the affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during his long illness, he sought omens and exorcisms, was misled by shamans, and petitioned to reduce his rank to avert calamity.

sentences.zh: 是年，凡七上章讓司空，復為檢校左僕射。

translations.literal: That year, in all seven times he submitted memorials declining Minister of Works, and again became Acting Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: That year he seven times petitioned to resign as Minister of Works and was restored as Acting Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年卒，時年六十二，廢朝三日，贈太保，賻以布帛米粟有差。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged sixty-two; court was suspended three days; posthumously granted Grand Tutor; condolence gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were graded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenyuan 10 at sixty-two. Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously named Grand Tutor, and graded gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain were sent.

sentences.zh: 抱真薨之日，其子殿中侍御史緘匿喪不發。

translations.literal: On the day Baozhen died, his son Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Jian concealed the death and did not announce the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Baozhen died, his son Jian, a palace censor, concealed the death and kept the mourning secret.

sentences.zh: 營田副使盧會昌令抱真從甥元仲經潛與緘謀，其明日，將吏會集，仲經詐為抱真令曰：「吾疾甚，不能蒞職，今令緘掌軍事，諸軍善佐之。

translations.literal: Garrison-fields Vice Commissioner Lu Huichang had Baozhen's cousin Yuan Zhongjing secretly plot with Jian; the next day when generals and officials assembled, Zhongjing falsely spoke as Baozhen's order: "My illness is severe; I cannot attend to duties; now I order Jian to take military affairs—let all armies well assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huichang, deputy commissioner of garrison fields, had Baozhen’s cousin Yuan Zhongjing plot with Jian in secret. The next day, when officers assembled, Zhongjing forged an order in Baozhen’s name: "I am gravely ill and cannot command; Jian will take the army—support him well.

sentences.zh: 」節度副使李說及諸將吏俯首，皆曰：「諾」。

translations.literal: " Vice military commissioner Li Yue and all generals and officials bowed their heads and all said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: " Vice commissioner Li Yue and the officers bowed and assented.

sentences.zh: 須臾，緘盛服而出，眾皆拜之，緘乃悉府藏頒賞軍士。

translations.literal: Shortly, Jian in full dress came out; the mass all bowed to him; Jian then emptied the treasury stores to distribute rewards to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly Jian appeared in full regalia; everyone bowed to him, and he emptied the treasury to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 盧會昌仍詐為抱真表，請以職事付緘。

translations.literal: Lu Huichang again forged a memorial as Baozhen, requesting that official duties be given to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huichang forged another memorial asking that command be transferred to Jian.

sentences.zh: 翌日，又令諸將連奏請緘領軍。

translations.literal: The next day he again had the generals submit linked memorials requesting Jian lead the army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the generals submitted joint petitions asking that Jian take command.

sentences.zh: 上已聞真疾病，請見明日。

translations.literal: The emperor had already heard of Baozhen's serious illness; they requested an audience tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had heard Baozhen was seriously ill; they claimed he would appear at court the next day.

sentences.zh: 如此者凡三日，緘乃出造中使，左右皆陳兵，甚嚴備。

translations.literal: Thus for three days in all; then Jian came out to visit the palace envoy; left and right all arrayed troops, very strictly prepared.
translations.idiomatic: This went on for three days. Then Jian went to see the palace envoy, flanked by armed guards in strict formation.

sentences.zh: 中使謂緘曰：「朝廷已知相公薨歿，令以兵務屬延貴，侍御宜歸發喪行服也。

translations.literal: The envoy said to Jian: "The court already knows the lord has died; it orders that military affairs belong to Yanguì; Attendant, you should return to announce the mourning and observe the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy told Jian, "The court knows your father is dead and has assigned the army to Yanguì. You should go home, announce the death, and observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 」緘愕然，出謂諸將曰：「有詔不許緘掌事，諸公意若何？

translations.literal: " Jian was startled; coming out he said to the generals: "There is an edict not permitting Jian to hold affairs—what is your gentlemen's intent?
translations.idiomatic: " Jian was stunned. He went out and asked the generals, "The edict forbids me to command—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」將吏莫有對者。

translations.literal: " None of the generals and officials had a reply.
translations.idiomatic: " No officer spoke up.

sentences.zh: 緘懼而退，遽以使印及管鑰歸監軍。

translations.literal: Jian, fearing, withdrew; hastily with the envoy seal and keys returned them to the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Jian withdrew in fear and hastily returned the commissioner’s seal and keys to the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 是日，乃發喪，畢一哭。

translations.literal: That day they announced the mourning; when finished, one cry.
translations.idiomatic: That day they announced the death and performed a single round of mourning.

sentences.zh: 中使召延貴，以口詔令視事，趣遣緘赴東都。

translations.literal: The palace envoy summoned Yanguì; with oral edict ordered him to take charge of affairs, urging Jian to go to the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy summoned Yanguì, orally ordered him to assume command, and hurried Jian off to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 元仲經逃於外，延貴捕得殺之。

translations.literal: Yuan Zhongjing fled outside; Yanguì captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhongjing fled; Yanguì captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 既歸罪仲經，盧會昌得不坐。

translations.literal: Having attributed guilt to Zhongjing, Lu Huichang escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Blame was pinned on Zhongjing, and Lu Huichang went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 緘初謀亂，遣裨將陳榮詐以文書告成德節度使王武俊，求假財帛，武俊大怒曰：「吾與汝府公善者，冀恭王命，非同惡也。

translations.literal: When Jian first plotted disorder, he sent subordinate general Chen Rong with a forged document to inform Chengde military commissioner Wang Wujun, requesting borrowed wealth and goods. Wujun was greatly angry and said: "I and your father's lord were on good terms, hoping to respect the king's command—not joining evil together.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian first plotted rebellion, he sent Chen Rong with a forged letter to Wang Wujun of Chengde asking for money and supplies. Wujun raged: "Your father and I were friends who honored the throne—we were not partners in treason.

sentences.zh: 今聞已亡，孰詐令其子而不俟朝旨耶？

translations.literal: Now I hear he is already dead—who falsely ordered his son without awaiting court decree?
translations.idiomatic: Now that he is dead, who dares put his son in command without awaiting the court?

sentences.zh: 何敢告我，況有求也！

translations.literal: How dare you inform me, moreover with a request!
translations.idiomatic: How dare you approach me—and with a request at that!

sentences.zh: 」乃囚陳榮而遣使讓緘焉。

translations.literal: " He then imprisoned Chen Rong and sent an envoy to reproach Jian.
translations.idiomatic: " He imprisoned Chen Rong and sent an envoy to rebuke Jian.

sentences.zh: 王虔休王虔休，字君佐，汝州梁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu. Wang Qianxiu, style Junzuo, was a native of Liang in Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu, courtesy name Junzuo, was from Liang in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 本名延貴。

translations.literal: His original name was Yanguì.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yanguì.

sentences.zh: 少涉獵書籍，鄉里間以信義畏慕之，尤好武藝。

translations.literal: In youth he dabbled in books; in village and hamlet he was feared and admired for faith and righteousness; he especially loved martial arts.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he read widely; neighbors respected him for integrity and admired his martial skill.

sentences.zh: 大曆中，汝州刺史李深用之為將。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, Ruzhou Prefect Li Shen employed him as a general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era, Ruzhou prefect Li Shen made him a commander.

sentences.zh: 久之，澤潞節度李抱真聞名，厚以財帛招之，累授兵馬使押衙。

translations.literal: After a long while, Ze-Lu commissioner Li Baozhen heard his fame and richly recruited him with goods and silk; he was repeatedly appointed army horse commissioner and guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen of Ze and Lu heard of him and recruited him with rich gifts, appointing him repeatedly as army horse commissioner and guard officer.

sentences.zh: 建中初，抱真統兵馬與諸將征討河北，其雙岡、水寨營等陣，虔休攻戰居多，擢為步軍都虞候，累加兼御史中丞、大夫，賜實封百戶。

translations.literal: Early in Jianzhong, Baozhen led troops with other generals to campaign in Hebei; at Shuanggang, Shuizhai camp, and other arrays Qianxiu was foremost in attack; he was promoted to chief commander of the infantry army, repeatedly added concurrent Vice Censor-in-chief and Grandee, and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong he followed Baozhen against Hebei and distinguished himself at Shuanggang and other battles; he became chief infantry commander, rose to Vice Censor-in-chief and Grandee, and received a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 洎抱真卒，裨將元仲經等議立抱真子緘，軍中擾亂，虔休正色言於眾曰：「軍州是天子軍州，將帥闕，合待朝命，何乃云云，妄生異意！

translations.literal: When Baozhen died, subordinate generals Yuan Zhongjing and others discussed installing Baozhen's son Jian; the army was in turmoil. Qianxiu with stern countenance said to the mass: "Army districts belong to the Son of Heaven; if commanders are lacking, we should await court decree—why all this talk, rashly giving rise to different intent!
translations.idiomatic: When Baozhen died, Yuan Zhongjing and others tried to install his son Jian. As the army wavered, Qianxiu sternly told the troops, "These garrisons belong to the Son of Heaven. If the commander is gone, we await the court—why entertain private schemes?

sentences.zh: 」軍中服從其言，由是竟免潰亂。

translations.literal: " The army obeyed his words; thereby they ultimately escaped collapse and chaos.
translations.idiomatic: " The troops obeyed him, and a mutiny was averted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知而嘉之，以邕王為昭義節度觀察大使，授虔休潞州左司馬，依前兼御史大夫，掌留後，仍賜名虔休。

translations.literal: The court, knowing and praising this, made the Prince of Yong king the Zhaoyi observation grand ambassador; appointed Qianxiu Left Major of Lu prefecture, as before concurrently Censor Grandee, holding the acting commission, and still granted the name Qianxiu.
translations.idiomatic: The court commended him, named the Prince of Yong observation ambassador for Zhaoyi, made Qianxiu Left Major of Lu with concurrent rank as Censor Grandee and acting commissioner, and granted him the name Qianxiu.

sentences.zh: 號令安撫。

translations.literal: His orders soothed and settled.
translations.idiomatic: His orders restored calm.

sentences.zh: 軍州大理。

translations.literal: The army district was greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: The command was thoroughly pacified.

sentences.zh: 二歲，遷潞州長史、昭義軍節度、澤潞磁邢洺觀察使，尋加檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: After two years he was moved to Chief Administrator of Lu, Zhaoyi Army military commissioner, and observation commissioner of Ze, Lu, Ci, Xing, and Ming; soon added Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became chief administrator of Lu, Zhaoyi military commissioner, and observation commissioner over Ze, Lu, Ci, Xing, and Ming, and soon Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 貞元十五年卒，年六十二。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhenyuan he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenyuan 15 at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，贈左僕射，賻以布帛米粟。

translations.literal: Court was suspended three days; posthumously granted Left Vice Director; condolence gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously named Left Vice Director, with gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain.

sentences.zh: 虔休性恭勤，儉省節用，管內州倉庾皆積糧儲，可支軍人數歲。

translations.literal: Qianxiu's nature was respectful and diligent, frugal and sparing in expenditure; within his command the prefectural granaries all accumulated grain stores sufficient to supply the army for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu was respectful, diligent, and frugal; granaries throughout his command held enough grain to feed the army for years.

sentences.zh: 又嘗撰《誕聖樂曲》以進，其表曰：

translations.literal: He also once composed the "Birth of the Sage" musical piece to present; his memorial said:
translations.idiomatic: He also composed the "Birth of the Sage" suite and presented it with a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 先時，有太常樂工劉玠流落至潞州，虔休因令造此曲以進，今《中和樂》起此也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Music Master worker Liu Jie had drifted to Luzhou; Qianxiu therefore had him compose this piece to present; today's "Zhonghe Music" begins from this.
translations.idiomatic: A court musician named Liu Jie had drifted to Luzhou; Qianxiu had him compose the piece. The later "Music of Central Harmony" originated here.

sentences.zh: 盧從史盧從史，其先自元魏已來，冠冕頗盛。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi. Lu Congshi's ancestors from the Northern Wei onward had caps and crowns quite flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi came from a family that had held high office since the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 父虔，少孤，好學，舉進士，歷御史府三院、刑部郎中、江汝二州刺史、秘書監。

translations.literal: His father Lu Qian, orphaned young, loved learning, passed the jinshi examination, and served in the three bureaus of the Censorate, as a director in the Ministry of Justice, as prefect of Jiang and Ru, and as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lu Qian, orphaned early, was a jinshi who served in the Censorate, the Ministry of Justice, as prefect of Jiang and Ru, and as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從史少矜力，習騎射，游澤、潞間，節度使李長榮用為大將。

translations.literal: Congshi in youth relied on strength, studied mounted archery, roamed between Ze and Lu, and military commissioner Li Changrong used him as a great general.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Congshi prided himself on strength, mastered horsemanship and archery, and roamed Ze and Lu until Li Changrong made him a senior commander.

sentences.zh: 德宗中歲，每命節制，必令採訪本軍為其所歸者。

translations.literal: In Dezong's middle years, whenever appointing military commissioners, he always ordered inquiry into whom the native army would follow.
translations.idiomatic: In his middle reign Dezong always asked which commander the local troops would accept before appointing a commissioner.

sentences.zh: 長榮卒，從史因軍情，且善迎奉中使，得授昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Changrong died, Congshi, relying on army sentiment and being skilled at welcoming palace envoys, received appointment as Zhaoyi Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Changrong died, Congshi won army support and court favor by courting palace envoys, and was made Zhaoyi military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漸狂恣不道，至奪部將妻妾，而辯給矯妄，從事孔戡等以言直不從引去。

translations.literal: He gradually became wildly unrestrained and lawless, even seizing his officers' wives and concubines; he was glib and falsely arrogant; aides Kong Kan and others, because their straight words were not followed, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He grew arrogant and lawless, even seizing his officers’ wives; glib and deceitful, he drove away aides such as Kong Kan when they spoke plainly.

sentences.zh: 前年丁父憂，朝旨未議起復，屬王士真卒，從史竊獻誅承宗計，以希上意，用是起授，委其成功。

translations.literal: The year before he completed mourning for his father; court had not yet discussed recall from mourning; when Wang Shizhen died, Congshi secretly presented a plan to execute Chengzong to win the emperor's favor; thereby he was recalled and appointed, entrusted with success.
translations.idiomatic: While still in mourning for his father, he secretly proposed killing Wang Chengzong after Shizhen’s death to please the throne; recalled from mourning, he was entrusted with the campaign.

sentences.zh: 及詔下討賊，兵出，逗留不進，陰與承宗通謀，令軍士潛懷賊號，又高其芻粟之價，售於度支，諷朝廷求宰相；

translations.literal: When the edict to campaign against the rebel was issued and troops marched out, he lingered without advancing, secretly conspired with Chengzong, had soldiers secretly keep rebel titles, also raised prices on fodder and grain and sold to the Finance Commission, and insinuated to the court a request for the chancellorship;
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign edict came he marched out but stalled, secretly dealing with Chengzong, letting troops keep rebel insignia, inflating fodder prices sold to the Finance Commission, and hinting that he should be made chancellor;

sentences.zh: 且誣奏諸軍與賊通，兵不可進。

translations.literal: and falsely memorialized that the various armies communicated with the rebels so troops could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: and falsely reported that other armies were colluding with the rebels so the campaign could not proceed.

sentences.zh: 上深患之。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 護軍中尉吐突承璀將神策兵與之對壘，從史往往過其營博戲。

translations.literal: Army Protector Commandant Tutu Chenghui led Shence troops to face him in camp; Congshi often passed his camp to gamble.
translations.idiomatic: Army Protector Tutu Chenghui camped against him with the Shence guard; Congshi often visited his camp to gamble.

sentences.zh: 從史沓貪好得，承璀出寶帶、奇玩以炫燿之，時其愛悅而遺焉，從史喜甚，日益狎。

translations.literal: Congshi was greedy and loved gain; Chenghui produced jeweled belts and curious playthings to dazzle him, sometimes what he loved and delighted in he gave as gifts; Congshi was very pleased and daily grew more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy Congshi was dazzled when Chenghui displayed jeweled belts and curios and gave him what he coveted; their intimacy deepened daily.

sentences.zh: 上知其事，取裴垍之謀，因戒承璀伺其來博，揖語，幕下伏壯士，突起，持捽出帳後縛之，內車中，馳以赴闕。

translations.literal: The emperor knew of this matter and took Pei Ji’s stratagem; he therefore warned Chenghui to watch for when Congshi came to gamble, bow and speak, with strong men hidden below the tent who would spring up, seize and drag him out behind the tent and bind him, put him inside a carriage, and gallop to present at court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted Pei Ji’s plan and told Chenghui: when Congshi came to gamble, greet him while braves hidden in the tent seized, bound, and hustled him into a carriage bound for the capital.

sentences.zh: 從者驚亂，斬十數人，余號令乃定，且宣諭密詔，追赴闕庭。

translations.literal: His followers were startled and in disorder; more than ten were beheaded; the rest only then settled under orders, and the secret edict was proclaimed, urging pursuit to the court.
translations.idiomatic: His escort panicked; a dozen were killed before order was restored and the secret edict announced that he was being taken to court.

sentences.zh: 都將烏重胤素懷忠順，乃嚴戒其軍，眾不敢動。

translations.literal: Chief commander Wu Zhongyin had long harbored loyalty and obedience; he therefore strictly warned his army, and the mass dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: Chief commander Wu Zhongyin, ever loyal, strictly restrained the troops, and none stirred.

sentences.zh: 會夜，使疾驅，未明出境，道路人莫知。

translations.literal: It happened at night; they were made to drive swiftly; before dawn they left the border; people on the road did not know.
translations.idiomatic: They raced through the night and crossed the border before dawn; travelers on the road knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 元和五年四月，制曰：

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuanhe, an edict said:
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yuanhe 5 an edict declared:

sentences.zh: 子繼宗等四人並貶嶺外。

translations.literal: His sons Jizong and the other four were all demoted beyond the Ling ranges.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Jizong and three others were all banished to the far south.

sentences.zh: 李芃李芃，字茂初，趙郡人也。

translations.literal: Li Peng. Li Peng, style Maochu, was a native of Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Li Peng, courtesy name Maochu, was from Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 解褐上邽主簿，三遷試大理評事，攝監察御史、山南東道觀察支使。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the sackcloth he was Shanggui registrar; after three promotions he was trial reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, acting Investigating Censor and staff officer of the Shannan east circuit observation commission.
translations.idiomatic: He began as registrar of Shanggui, rose through three posts to trial reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review, then served as acting censor and staff officer on the Shannan east observation commission.

sentences.zh: 嚴武為京兆尹，舉為長安尉。

translations.literal: When Yan Wu was Jingzhao magistrate, he recommended him as Chang'an bailiff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Wu was magistrate of Jingzhao, he recommended Peng as bailiff of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 李勉為江西觀察使，署奏秘書郎、兼監察御史，為判官。

translations.literal: When Li Mian was Jiangxi observation commissioner, he memorialized appointing him Secretariat Gentleman, concurrently Investigating Censor, as judge.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian, as Jiangxi observation commissioner, appointed him Secretariat Gentleman and concurrent censor, with duties as his judge.

sentences.zh: 永泰初，轉兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Early in Yongtai he was transferred to concurrently Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongtai he became a palace attendant censor as well.

sentences.zh: 時宣、饒二州人方清、陳莊聚眾據山洞，西絕江路，劫商旅以為亂。

translations.literal: At that time in Xuan and Rao prefectures, Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang gathered masses and held mountain caves, cutting the river road to the west and robbing merchants and travelers to make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuan and Rao, Fang Qing and Chen Zhuang gathered bands in mountain caves, cut the western river route, and plundered merchants.

sentences.zh: 芃乃請於秋浦置州，守其要地，以破其謀。

translations.literal: Peng then requested establishing a prefecture at Qiupu to guard the strategic place and break their plot.
translations.idiomatic: Peng proposed creating a prefecture at Qiupu to hold the choke point and break their plans.

sentences.zh: 李勉然其計，以聞，代宗嘉之，以宣州之秋浦、青陽、饒州之至德置池州焉。

translations.literal: Li Mian approved his plan and reported it; Emperor Daizong praised it; from Xuanzhou's Qiupu and Qingyang and Raozhou's Zhide he established Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian approved and reported the plan; Daizong praised it and formed Chizhou from Qiupu and Qingyang of Xuan and Zhide of Rao.

sentences.zh: 芃攝行事，無幾，乃兼侍御史。

translations.literal: Peng acted in administrative affairs; before long he was also made Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Peng administered the new prefecture and soon added the title of attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 居無何，魏少游代勉為使，復署奏檢校虞部員外郎，賜金紫，為都團練副使。

translations.literal: After not long, Wei Shaoyou replaced Mian as commissioner; he again memorialized appointing him Acting Vice Director of the Parks Bureau, granted gold and purple, as deputy metropolitan training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Shaoyou succeeded Mian, Peng was named Acting Vice Director of the Parks Bureau, given gold and purple insignia, and made deputy training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 頃之，攝江州刺史，州人便之。

translations.literal: Shortly he acted as Jiangzhou prefect; the people of the prefecture found him convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he acted as prefect of Jiangzhou, to the people’s benefit.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，免喪，永平軍節度李勉署奏檢校工部郎中、兼侍御史，為判官，尋攝陳州刺史。

translations.literal: He completed mourning for his mother; when mourning ended, Yongping Army commissioner Li Mian memorialized appointing him Acting Director in the Ministry of Works, concurrently Attendant Censor, as judge; soon he acted as Chenzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother’s mourning, Li Mian of Yongping named him Acting Director in the Ministry of Works and attendant censor on his staff, then acting prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲中，即值李靈曜反於汴州，勉署芃兼亳州防禦使，練達軍事，兵備甚肅；

translations.literal: Within the year he encountered Li Lingyao rebelling at Bianzhou; Mian appointed Peng concurrently Bozhou defense commissioner; skilled in military affairs, armaments were very strict;
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Lingyao rebelled at Bianzhou; Mian made Peng concurrent defense commissioner of Bo, where he drilled the army to peak readiness;

sentences.zh: 又開陳、潁運路，以通漕輓。

translations.literal: he also opened the Chen and Ying transport routes to connect grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: and reopened the Chen and Ying transport routes for grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，授檢校太常少卿、兼御史中丞、河陽三城鎮遏使。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded, he was appointed Acting Vice Director of the Grand Music Office, concurrently Vice Censor-in-chief, and suppressor of the Heyang Three Cities.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded, Peng became Acting Vice Director of the Grand Music Office, Vice Censor-in-chief, and commissioner for the Heyang Three Cities.

sentences.zh: 撫勞備至，資廩善者，必先軍士。

translations.literal: In comforting and toil he was utterly thorough; good provisions and granaries were always given first to the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for the troops exhaustively and always gave the best supplies to the soldiers first.

sentences.zh: 間一年，為節度使路嗣恭之副，加檢校左庶子、河陽三城懷州節度觀察使，以東畿汜水等五縣隸焉。

translations.literal: After one year he became deputy to military commissioner Lu Sigong, added Acting Left Household Son, Heyang Three Cities and Huaizhou military observation commissioner, with five counties of the eastern capital region including Sishui placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became deputy to Lu Sigong, Acting Left Household Son, and military observation commissioner of Heyang, the Three Cities, and Huaizhou, with five eastern capital counties added to his command.

sentences.zh: 時河南北連大兵，詔益以神策、汝、陝之師。

translations.literal: At that time north and south of the Yellow River were linked in great armies; an edict added Shence, Ru, and Shan troops.
translations.idiomatic: With major armies active north and south of the Yellow River, edicts reinforced him with Shence troops and forces from Ru and Shan.

sentences.zh: 芃進收新鄉、共城，遂圍衛州。

translations.literal: Peng advanced and recovered Xinxiang and Gongcheng, then besieged Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Peng retook Xinxiang and Gongcheng and besieged Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔與河東節度馬燧等諸軍破田悅於洹水，以功加檢校兵部尚書，累封開郡王，實封一百戶。

translations.literal: The next year an edict joined him with Hedong commissioner Ma Sui and other armies to defeat Tian Yue at the Huan River; for merit he was added Acting Minister of War, repeatedly enfeoffed as Prince of Kai commandery with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined Ma Sui and others to crush Tian Yue on the Huan River; for merit he became Acting Minister of War and was enfeoffed as Prince of Kai with a fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 進圍悅於魏州，將符璘以精騎五百夜降，芃耳開營以納之。

translations.literal: Advancing to besiege Yue at Weizhou, general Fu Lin with five hundred crack horsemen surrendered by night; Peng personally opened the camp to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the siege of Weizhou, general Fu Lin defected at night with five hundred horsemen; Peng himself opened the camp to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 明日，歸璘於招討使。

translations.literal: The next day he returned Lin to the pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent Lin on to the pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上居奉天，斂軍還。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Fengtian, he gathered his army and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor withdrew to Fengtian, he gathered his troops and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 興元初，檢校右僕射，無何，以疾固讓罷歸。

translations.literal: Early in Xingyuan he was Acting Right Vice Director; before long, because of illness he firmly declined and was dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xingyuan he became Acting Right Vice Director; soon illness led him to resign and return home.

sentences.zh: 芃將請告，謂所親曰：「今年夏被蝗旱，人主厭兵革，然則天下城壘堅厚矣，戈鋋銛利矣，以力勝之，則有得失，其可盡乎！

translations.literal: As Peng was about to request leave, he said to those close to him: "This summer we suffered locusts and drought; the ruler is weary of arms—yet the realm's walls and ramparts are thick and strong, spears and blades sharp. To overcome by force has gains and losses; can it be exhausted!
translations.idiomatic: When Peng sought leave, he told his intimates, "Locusts and drought struck this summer; the emperor is weary of war. Walls are strong and weapons sharp—victory by force alone cannot be final.

sentences.zh: 除弊之急，莫先德化，循而理之，斯易致耳。

translations.literal: The urgent task in removing abuses is none before moral transformation; follow and govern it—this is easily achieved.
translations.idiomatic: The urgent cure is moral governance; rule patiently and peace comes easily.

sentences.zh: 方鎮之戴翼時主，宜先退讓，貪權持祿，吾所不取也。

translations.literal: For frontier commissioners to support the timely ruler, they should first yield; to covet power and hold salary—that I do not take.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier lords should support the throne by yielding first; clinging to power and pay I will not do.

sentences.zh: 吾既疾病，豈能言而不踐乎！

translations.literal: Since I am already ill, how can I speak and not practice it!
translations.idiomatic: I am ill—how can I preach this and not act on it!

sentences.zh: 」乃手疏乞罷。

translations.literal: " He then personally wrote a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: " He wrote a personal memorial asking to resign.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年卒，年六十四，廢朝一日，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan he died, aged sixty-four; court was suspended one day; posthumously granted Crown Prince Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenyuan 1 at sixty-four. Court was suspended one day; he was posthumously named Crown Prince Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 李澄李澄，遼東襄平人，隋蒲山公寬之後也，居京兆。

translations.literal: Li Cheng. Li Cheng was a native of Xiangping in Liaodong, a descendant of Sui's Duke of Pushan, Li Kuan, and dwelt in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cheng, from Xiangping in Liaodong, was a descendant of Sui’s Duke of Pushan, Li Kuan, and lived in the capital region.

sentences.zh: 父鎬，清江太守，以澄贈工部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Hao was Qingjiang prefect; because of Cheng he was posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hao had been prefect of Qingjiang; Cheng’s honors brought him a posthumous appointment as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 澄以武藝為偏將，累除試將作監，隸於江淮都統李峘。

translations.literal: Cheng, through martial arts, became a junior officer; repeatedly removed and appointed trial Director of Palace Construction; he was subordinate to Jiang-Huai overall commander Li Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng entered service as a junior officer through martial skill, rose to trial Director of Palace Construction, and served under Li Qian, overall commander of Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 建中初，以檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞隸於永平軍節度使李勉。

translations.literal: Early in Jianzhong he was Acting Crown Prince Guest and concurrently Vice Censor-in-chief, subordinate to Yongping Army commissioner Li Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong he served Li Mian of Yongping as Acting Crown Prince Guest and Vice Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 及勉移理汴州，乃奏澄為滑州刺史。

translations.literal: When Mian moved administration to Bianzhou, he memorialized making Cheng Huazhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian moved his headquarters to Bianzhou, he recommended Cheng as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 四年冬，李希烈陷汴州，勉奔歸行在，澄遂以城降希烈，偽署尚書令，兼滑州永平軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year Li Xilie took Bianzhou; Mian fled back to the imperial camp; Cheng then surrendered the city to Xilie, who falsely appointed him Minister Director, concurrently Huazhou and Yongping Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Li Xilie seized Bianzhou; Mian fled to the emperor’s camp, and Cheng surrendered Hua to Xilie, who made him Minister Director and military commissioner of Hua and Yongping.

sentences.zh: 興元元年春，澄密令親信人盧融間道賚表達於奉天，上嘉之，乃以帛詔藏於蠟丸中，加澄刑部尚書，兼汴州刺史、汴滑節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xingyuan, Cheng secretly ordered trusted man Lu Rong by hidden route to deliver a memorial to Fengtian; the emperor praised it and placed the silk edict hidden in a wax pellet, adding Cheng Minister of Justice, concurrently Bianzhou prefect and Bian-Hua military observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Xingyuan 1, Cheng sent Lu Rong by secret route with a loyal memorial to Fengtian. The emperor approved and hid an edict in a wax ball, naming Cheng Minister of Justice, prefect of Bian, and commissioner of Bian and Hua.

sentences.zh: 澄秘而未宣，乃集州兵嚴加訓習。

translations.literal: Cheng kept it secret and did not proclaim it; he then gathered prefectural troops and strictly trained them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng kept the edict secret and drilled the prefectural troops rigorously.

sentences.zh: 希烈頗疑之，乃令養子六百人戍之，以虞其變。

translations.literal: Xilie was quite suspicious and therefore ordered six hundred adopted sons to garrison it, to guard against his change.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie grew suspicious and posted six hundred of his adopted sons to garrison the city against defection.

sentences.zh: 希烈苦攻寧陵，邀澄率其眾至石柱。

translations.literal: Xilie bitterly attacked Ningling and invited Cheng to lead his masses to Shizhu.
translations.idiomatic: While Xilie pressed the siege of Ningling, he summoned Cheng and his troops to Shizhu.

sentences.zh: 澄令縱火焚營，而偽遁，誘六百人因驚行剽而加其罪，果大俘掠，悉令斬之以告。

translations.literal: Cheng ordered setting fire to burn the camp while feigning flight, luring the six hundred because startled into marching to plunder and adding their crime; indeed they greatly captured and looted; he ordered all beheaded to report.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng set fire to the camp and pretended to flee; the six hundred, startled, looted the countryside. He charged them with pillage, had them all beheaded, and reported to Xilie.

sentences.zh: 希烈不能窮詰焉。

translations.literal: Xilie could not thoroughly investigate it.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie could not pursue the matter further.

sentences.zh: 無凡，希烈遣其將翟暉等寇陳州，久之未復。

translations.literal: Before long Xilie sent his generals Zhai Hui and others to raid Chenzhou; for a long while they did not return.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xilie sent Zhai Hui and others against Chenzhou, and they were long absent.

sentences.zh: 是歲十月，澄以汴州兵寡，度希烈不能制己，又會中官薛盈珍持節且至，加檢校兵部尚書，封武威郡王，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: That year in the tenth month, Cheng judged Bianzhou troops few, estimated Xilie could not control him, and also met palace envoy Xue Yingzhen bearing the staff about to arrive; he was added Acting Minister of War, enfeoffed Prince of Wuwei commandery, granted substantive fief five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: That October, with few troops at Bian and believing Xilie could not restrain him, Cheng also learned that envoy Xue Yingzhen was coming with new honors—Acting Minister of War, Prince of Wuwei, and a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 澄乃乘勢力焚賊旌節，誓眾歸國。

translations.literal: Cheng then seized the momentum, burned the rebel banners and staffs, and swore the masses to return to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng seized the moment, burned the rebel standards, and rallied his men to return to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及十一月，希烈既失澄，又聞翟暉大敗，由是奔歸蔡州。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month, Xilie having lost Cheng and also hearing Zhai Hui was greatly defeated, thereby fled back to Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: By November, having lost Cheng and hearing of Zhai Hui’s defeat, Xilie fled back to Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 澄遽率眾將復汴州，屯於城北門，恇怯不敢進。

translations.literal: Cheng hastily led his masses intending to recover Bianzhou, encamped at the north city gate, but in fear and timidity dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng hurried to retake Bianzhou but camped at the north gate, too timid to enter.

sentences.zh: 及宣武軍節度使劉洽師至城東門，賊將田懷珍開關以納之。

translations.literal: When Xuanyi Army commissioner Liu Qia's troops reached the east city gate, rebel general Tian Huaizhen opened the pass to admit them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Qia of Xuanyi reached the east gate, rebel general Tian Huaizhen opened the gates to admit him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，澄方自北入，洽已據子城。

translations.literal: The next day Cheng only then entered from the north; Qia had already seized the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Cheng entered from the north, but Qia already held the inner city.

sentences.zh: 澄乃舍於浚儀縣，兩軍將士，日有忿競，不自安。

translations.literal: Cheng then lodged in Junyi county; the two armies' officers and soldiers daily had angry rivalry and were not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng lodged in Junyi county while the two armies quarreled daily and grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 會鄭州賊將孫液通款於澄，澄遣其子清赴之。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhengzhou rebel general Sun Ye communicated terms to Cheng; Cheng sent his son Qing to go there.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengzhou rebel Sun Ye offered terms to Cheng, Cheng sent his son Qing.

sentences.zh: 先是，河陽軍節度使李芃遣其將雍顥攻鄭州，顥所過縱掠，液拒之尤固；

translations.literal: Earlier, Heyang Army commissioner Li Peng had sent his general Yong Hao to attack Zhengzhou; wherever Hao passed he allowed looting; Ye resisted him especially firmly;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Peng of Heyang had sent Yong Hao against Zhengzhou; Hao’s troops plundered as they marched, and Sun Ye resisted fiercely;

sentences.zh: 及清至，遂納之。

translations.literal: when Qing arrived, he then submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: when Qing arrived, Sun Ye submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 顥怒攻液，清以眾助之，殺登城者數十人，顥方引退，又焚陽武而歸。

translations.literal: Hao angrily attacked Ye; Qing with his masses assisted him, killing several dozen who climbed the walls; Hao only then withdrew, again burned Yangwu and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hao attacked in rage; Qing helped Sun Ye kill dozens of assailants on the walls; Hao withdrew, burned Yangwu, and retreated.

sentences.zh: 澄乃出赴鄭州，朝廷特授清檢校太子賓客、兼御史中丞，更名克寧。

translations.literal: Cheng then went out to Zhengzhou; the court specially appointed Qing Acting Crown Prince Guest, concurrently Vice Censor-in-chief, and changed his name to Kening.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng went to Zhengzhou; the court named Qing Acting Crown Prince Guest and Vice Censor-in-chief, changing his name to Kening.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年三月，就加澄檢校左僕射、義成軍鄭滑許等州節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhenyuan he was thereupon added Acting Left Vice Director and military commissioner of the Yicheng Army and the prefectures Zheng, Hua, Xu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhenyuan 1 Cheng was named Acting Left Vice Director and military commissioner of Yicheng and the Zheng, Hua, and Xu circuits.

sentences.zh: 二年卒，年五十四，廢朝一日，贈司空，賵布帛粟有差，仍令左散騎常侍歸崇敬充弔祭使，所緣喪葬，並勒官給。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged fifty-four; court was suspended one day; posthumously granted Minister of Works; condolence cloth, silk, and grain were graded; he was further ordered that Left Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Gui Jingchong serve as condolence envoy; all related mourning and burial were commanded to be supplied by the state.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year at fifty-four. Court halted for a day; he was posthumously named Minister of Works, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, and grain. Gui Jingchong was sent to mourn him, and all funeral costs were paid by the state.

sentences.zh: 澄實以八月癸未終，克寧秘之，以九月庚寅，欲自起視事。

translations.literal: Cheng in fact ended on guimwei in the eighth month; Kening concealed it; on gengyin in the ninth month he wished to rise himself and attend to affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng had actually died on the guimwei day of the eighth month; Kening kept it secret and on the gengyin day of the ninth month tried to take command himself.

sentences.zh: 其行軍司馬馬鉉不許，克寧陰遣殺之，乃墨絰而出，加卒於城門，將為不順。

translations.literal: His campaigning army vice director Ma Xuan would not permit it; Kening secretly sent men to kill him; then in black mourning he came out, added soldiers at the city gate, and was about to act rebelliously.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign vice director Ma Xuan refused; Kening had him murdered secretly, donned mourning, posted extra guards at the gates, and prepared to rebel.

sentences.zh: 劉洽出師屯於境上以制之，且使告諭切至，由是克寧不敢妄發，然道路絕商旅者凡十四五日。

translations.literal: Liu Qia led troops out and encamped on the border to restrain him, and also sent envoys with urgent admonition; thereby Kening dared not rashly act, yet travelers and merchants were cut off on the roads for fourteen or fifteen days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qia camped on the border to restrain him and sent stern warnings; Kening dared not move, but travel was cut off for fifteen days.

sentences.zh: 及賈躭代澄，克寧護喪將歸，乃悉索府中財貨，以夜出城，軍人從而剽奪，及明殆盡。

translations.literal: When Jia Dan replaced Cheng, Kening escorted the coffin intending to return; he then searched out all wealth and goods in the treasury, left the city by night, and soldiers followed in plundering; by dawn it was nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: When Jia Dan succeeded Cheng, Kening escorted the coffin home, stripped the treasury by night, and soldiers looted until dawn left little behind.

sentences.zh: 澄柩至京師，又賜克寧莊一所、錢千貫、粟麥二千石。

translations.literal: When Cheng's bier reached the capital, Kening was again granted one estate, one thousand strings of cash, and two thousand shi of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng’s coffin reached the capital, Kening was still granted an estate, a thousand strings of cash, and two thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 澄初封隴西郡公，進武威郡王，每上疏連稱二封，頗為時人所哂。

translations.literal: Cheng was first enfeoffed Duke of Longxi commandery, advanced to Prince of Wuwei commandery; in each memorial he linked both titles, and was much ridiculed by men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was first made Duke of Longxi, then Prince of Wuwei, and in memorials he cited both titles—a habit people mocked.

sentences.zh: 李元素李元素，字大朴，蒲山公密之孫。

translations.literal: Li Yuan Su. Li Yuan Su, style Dapu, was a grandson of Duke of Pushan, Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan Su, courtesy name Dapu, was a grandson of Li Mi, Duke of Pushan.

sentences.zh: 任侍御史，時杜亞為東都留守，惡大將令狐運，會盜發洛城之北，運適與其部下畋於北郊，亞意其為盜，遂執訊之，逮系者四十餘人。

translations.literal: He served as Attendant Censor; at that time Du Ya was eastern capital regent and hated great general Linghu Yun; it happened that bandits struck north of Luoyang; Yun happened to be hunting in the northern suburbs with his subordinates; Ya thought him the bandit, seized and interrogated him, and more than forty were arrested and bound.
translations.idiomatic: As an attendant censor, he served under Du Ya, regent of the eastern capital, who hated general Linghu Yun. When bandits struck north of Luoyang, Yun was hunting nearby; Du Ya arrested him and more than forty others.

sentences.zh: 監察御史楊寧按其事，亞以為不直，密表陳之，寧遂得罪。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Yang Ning examined the matter; Ya thought him not upright, secretly memorialized stating this, and Ning thereupon was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Yang Ning reviewed the case; Du Ya thought him biased, secretly denounced him, and Yang Ning was punished.

sentences.zh: 亞將逞其宿怒，且以得賊為功，上表指明運為盜之狀，上信而不疑。

translations.literal: Ya was about to vent his old anger and also take catching the bandits as merit; he memorialized specifying Yun's appearance as bandit; the emperor believed and did not doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya vented his old grudge and claimed credit for catching the bandits, memorializing that Yun was the culprit; the emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 宰臣以獄大宜審，奏請覆之，命元素就決，亞迎路以獄成告。

translations.literal: Chancellors, because the case was great and should be carefully examined, memorialized requesting review; Yuan Su was ordered to go and decide; Ya met him on the road announcing the case was already concluded.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors urged a review; Yuan Su was sent to decide. Du Ya met him on the road and said the case was already closed.

sentences.zh: 元素驗之五日，盡釋其囚以還。

translations.literal: Yuan Su examined it for five days and released all the prisoners to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Su investigated for five days and released every prisoner.

sentences.zh: 亞大驚，且怒，親追送，馬上責之，元素不答。

translations.literal: Ya was greatly startled and also angry; he personally pursued and saw him off, reproaching him from horseback; Yuan Su did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya was shocked and furious, rode after him reproaching him from horseback; Yuan Su did not answer.

sentences.zh: 亞遂上疏，又誣元素。

translations.literal: Ya then submitted a memorial again slandering Yuan Su.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ya memorialized again, slandering Yuan Su.

sentences.zh: 元素還奏，言未畢，上怒曰：「出俟命。

translations.literal: Yuan Su returned to report; before he finished speaking the emperor angrily said: "Go out and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Su reported back; before he finished, the emperor snapped, "Leave and await my orders.

sentences.zh: 」元素曰：「臣未盡詞。

translations.literal: " Yuan Su said: "Your subject has not finished his words.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Su said, "I have not finished, Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」上又曰：「且去」。

translations.literal: " The emperor again said: "Go for now."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said again, "Go now."

sentences.zh: 元素復奏曰：「一出不得復見陛下，乞容盡詞。

translations.literal: Yuan Su again reported: "Once I go out I cannot again see Your Majesty; I beg leave to finish my words.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Su pleaded, "If I leave now I may never see Your Majesty again—let me finish.

sentences.zh: 」上意稍緩，元素盡言運冤狀明白，上乃寤曰：「非卿，孰能辨之！

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind eased somewhat; Yuan Su fully stated Yun's wrongful situation clearly; the emperor then awakened and said: "Without you, who could distinguish it!
