translations.idiomatic: " The emperor relented; Yuan Su laid out Yun’s innocence clearly, and the emperor exclaimed, "Without you, who could have seen this!

sentences.zh: 」後數月，竟得其真賊，元素由是為時器重，遷給事中。

translations.literal: " Months later they finally got the true bandits; Yuan Su thereby was valued by the age and was moved to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: " Months later the real culprits were caught, and Yuan Su won wide esteem and promotion to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 時美官缺，必指元素。

translations.literal: Whenever a fine office was vacant, they always pointed to Yuan Su.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prestigious post opened, Yuan Su was the expected choice.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Assistant Director of the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: He became Right Assistant Director of the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 數月，鄭滑節度盧群卒，遂命元素兼御史大夫，鎮鄭滑，就加檢校工部尚書，在鎮稱理。

translations.literal: After several months Zheng-Hua commissioner Lu Qun died; Yuan Su was then ordered concurrently Censor Grandee, to garrison Zheng-Hua, thereupon added Acting Minister of Works; in the command he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Qun of Zheng-Hua died, Yuan Su was named Censor Grandee and commissioner, with Acting Minister of Works, and governed well.

sentences.zh: 元和初，征拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanhe he was summoned and appointed Censor Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he was summoned to the post of Censor Grandee.

sentences.zh: 自貞元中位缺，久難其人，至是元素以名望召拜，中外聳聽。

translations.literal: Since the Zhenyuan era the post had been vacant and for long it was hard to find the man; now Yuan Su was summoned and appointed for his fame; inside and outside the court all listened with raised attention.
translations.idiomatic: The post had been vacant since Zhenyuan; Yuan Su’s appointment by reputation drew attention throughout the court and realm.

sentences.zh: 及居位，一無修舉，但規求作相。

translations.literal: When he took the post, he had not a single achievement, but only plotted to become chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In office he accomplished nothing and only schemed to become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 久之，浸不得志，見客必曰：「無以某官散相疏也。

translations.literal: After long while he gradually did not get his wish; seeing guests he always said: "Do not let my office as scattered chancellor keep us distant.
translations.idiomatic: As time passed he grew frustrated and told every visitor, "Do not shun me because I am only a chancellor in name.

sentences.zh: 」見屬官必先拜，脂韋在列，大失人情。

translations.literal: " Seeing subordinate officials he always bowed first; oily flatterers stood in his ranks—he greatly lost human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed first to his own subordinates and kept sycophants about him—alienating everyone.

sentences.zh: 李錡為亂江南，遂授元素浙西道節度觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: When Li Qi rebelled in Jiangnan, Yuan Su was then appointed Zhexi circuit military observation and disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi rebelled in the south, Yuan Su was made military commissioner of the Zhexi circuit.

sentences.zh: 數月受代，入拜國子祭酒，尋遷太常卿，轉戶部尚書、判度支。

translations.literal: After several months he was replaced; he entered court as Director of the Directorate of Education; soon moved to Director of the Grand Music Office; transferred to Minister of Revenue and judged the Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After a few months he was replaced, became Director of the Imperial University, then Grand Music Director, then Minister of Revenue with charge of the Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 元素少孤，奉長姊友敬加於人，及其姊歿，沉悲遘疾，上疏懇辭，從之。

translations.literal: Yuan Su was orphaned young; he served his elder sister with friendship and respect beyond others; when his sister died he sank in grief and met illness; he submitted a earnest memorial requesting leave; it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he revered his elder sister; when she died he fell ill with grief, petitioned to resign, and was allowed to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 數月，以出妻免官。

translations.literal: After several months he was dismissed from office for divorcing his wife.
translations.idiomatic: Months later he was dismissed for divorcing his wife.

sentences.zh: 初，元素再娶妻王氏，石泉公方慶之孫，性柔弱，元素為郎官時娶之，甚禮重，及貴，溺情僕妾，遂薄之。

translations.literal: At first Yuan Su remarried Lady Wang, granddaughter of Duke of Shiquan Fang Qing; her nature was gentle and weak; when Yuan Su was a court gentleman he married her and greatly honored her; when he became eminent he doted on servant girls and concubines and therefore treated her lightly.
translations.idiomatic: He had remarried Lady Wang, granddaughter of Fang Qing, while still a junior official and treated her well; once powerful he favored concubines and neglected her.

sentences.zh: 且又無子，而前妻之子已長，無良，元素寢疾昏惑，聽譖遂出之，給與非厚。

translations.literal: Moreover she had no son, while the son by his former wife was already grown and without goodness; Yuan Su in bed illness was muddled, listened to slander and then expelled her; what was given was not generous.
translations.idiomatic: She bore no children; his grown son by a former wife was worthless. Ill and confused, he heeded slander, divorced her, and gave her a meager settlement.

sentences.zh: 妻族上訴，乃詔曰：「李元素病中上表，懇切披陳，雲『妻王氏，禮義殊乖，願與離絕』。

translations.literal: The wife's clan appealed upward; an edict then said: "Li Yuan Su in illness submitted a memorial earnestly laying bare, saying 'Wife Wang, ritual and righteousness greatly diverge; I wish to separate from her.'
translations.idiomatic: Her family appealed to the throne, which declared: "Li Yuan Su, while ill, petitioned that his wife Wang had violated ritual and he wished to divorce her.

sentences.zh: 初謂素有醜行，不能顯言，以其大官之家，所以令自處置。

translations.literal: At first it was thought she had long had shameful conduct and he could not state it plainly; because hers was a great official's household, he was therefore allowed to dispose of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: We first assumed she had long misbehaved and he could not say so openly; as she came from a great official family, he was allowed to handle it privately.

sentences.zh: 訪聞不曾告報妻族，亦無明過可書，蓋是中情不和，遂至於此。

translations.literal: On inquiry it was heard he had never informed the wife's clan, nor was there any clear fault that could be written; probably inner feelings were not harmonious, and it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Inquiry showed he never informed her family and no clear fault was found—only mutual estrangement brought this about.

sentences.zh: 脅以王命，當日遣歸，給送之間，又至單薄。

translations.literal: Coerced by the king's command, she was sent back the same day; in what was given for her send-off it was again meager.
translations.idiomatic: Under imperial pressure she was sent home the same day with a paltry settlement.

sentences.zh: 不唯王氏受辱，實亦朝情悉驚。

translations.literal: Not only did Lady Wang suffer insult; in truth court sentiment was entirely startled.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wang was shamed, and court opinion was shocked.

sentences.zh: 如此理家，合當懲責。

translations.literal: To manage a household thus deserves punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Such household conduct deserved punishment.

sentences.zh: 宜停官，仍令與王氏錢物，通所奏數滿五千貫。

translations.literal: He should be suspended from office; he is still ordered to give Lady Wang money and goods, in all reaching five thousand strings as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: He is dismissed from office and ordered to pay Lady Wang five thousand strings in all, as petitioned.

sentences.zh: 」元和五年卒，贈陝州大都督。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year of Yuanhe he died; posthumously granted Grand Governor of Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in Yuanhe 5 and was posthumously named Grand Governor of Shanzhou.

sentences.zh: 【贊】史臣曰：李抱玉、李抱真，以武勇之材，兼忠義之行，有唐之良將也。

translations.literal: [Praise] The historiographer says: Li Baoyu and Li Baozhen, with martial courage as material and together with loyal and righteous conduct, were good generals of the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: [Appraisal] The historiographer writes: Li Baoyu and Li Baozhen combined martial courage with loyal service—they were among the Tang’s finest generals.

sentences.zh: 且如農隙教潞人之射，數騎入武俊之營，非有奇謀，孰能如是。

translations.literal: Moreover, such as teaching the people of Lu to shoot in farming gaps, or entering Wujun's camp with several horsemen—without strange stratagems, who could be like this?
translations.idiomatic: Training Lu archers in farming seasons, or riding into Wang Wujun’s camp with a handful of men—without exceptional daring, who could do such things?

sentences.zh: 惜乎服食求仙，為藥所誤。

translations.literal: Alas that in taking elixirs and seeking immortality he was misled by medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Alas that Baozhen’s quest for immortality through elixirs destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 王虔休不黨僭命，有足可嘉；

translations.literal: Wang Qianxiu did not join the usurper's faction—there is enough to praise;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qianxiu refused to side with usurpers—praiseworthy;

sentences.zh: 盧從史動多懷奸，自貽伊戚。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi in his movements often harbored treachery and brought calamity on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi’s treachery brought ruin on himself.

sentences.zh: 芃則老也知足，澄則過而改圖。

translations.literal: Peng in old age knew sufficiency; Cheng after error changed his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Peng in old age knew when to be content; Cheng erred, then changed course.

sentences.zh: 元素為御史時，執德不回；

translations.literal: When Yuan Su was a censor he held to virtue and did not turn back;
translations.idiomatic: As a censor Yuan Su held firm to principle;

sentences.zh: 居大夫日，其心甚短。

translations.literal: in the days as Grandee his heart was very short.
translations.idiomatic: as Censor Grandee his ambitions proved petty.

sentences.zh: 因緣七出，益露醜聲，善少惡多，又何足算。

translations.literal: Because of the seven grounds for expulsion, he further exposed shameful reputation; good was few and evil many—what is there to reckon?
translations.idiomatic: His divorce on the seven grounds exposed his shame; virtues were few and faults many—little remains to his credit.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：抱玉、抱真，我朝良將。

translations.literal: The praise says: Baoyu and Baozhen—our dynasty's good generals.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: Baoyu and Baozhen—fine generals of our dynasty.

sentences.zh: 虔休之心，亦多可尚。

translations.literal: Qianxiu's heart also has much to be esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Qianxiu’s loyalty also deserves esteem.

sentences.zh: 史懷奸謀，芃將祿讓。

translations.literal: Shi harbored treacherous plots; Peng was about to yield salary and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Congshi plotted treason; Peng would yield his post and pay.

sentences.zh: 澄迷卻行，素貪一響。

translations.literal: Cheng was confused in retreating action; plain greed for one reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng wavered, then turned back—ever greedy for renown.

sentences.zh: 吾誰與欺，豈如忠諒。

translations.literal: Whom would I deceive—how could it compare to loyal sincerity?
translations.idiomatic: Whom would we deceive—better loyal candor every time.
